name: ToolWeaver: Weaving Collaborative Semantics for Scalable Tool Use in Large Language Models
venue: ICLR 2026 (accepted; preprint arXiv:2601.21947, cs.AI, submitted 2026-01-29; DBLP: journals/corr/abs-2601-21947)
authors_affiliation: Bowen Fang, Wen Ye, Yunyue Su, Jinghao Zhang, Qiang Liu, Yesheng Liu, Jiabing Yang, Xin Sun, Shu Wu (corresponding), Baole Wei (corresponding), Liang Wang. Primary affiliation: New Laboratory of Pattern Recognition (NLPR), Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences (CASIA); also School of Artificial Intelligence, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences; Zhongguancun Academy; Zhongguancun Institute of Artificial Intelligence.
code_url: https://github.com/Fwibo/ToolWeaver (stated in paper footnote: 'Data and code are available at')
maintained_repo_url: https://github.com/Fwibo/ToolWeaver (single project repo accompanying the paper; not a continuously-updated leaderboard) [uncertain]
task_domain: Tool-use: generative tool learning for large-scale tool selection and end-to-end tool-augmented agent task completion over ~47k real-world APIs (ToolBench/RapidAPI).
problem_setting: Interactive, single-agent tool use with supervised fine-tuning. Given a user query and a massive tool corpus D (46,985 APIs from ToolBench), an LLM agent must iteratively (1) plan a step, (2) select a tool, (3) generate its parameters, and (4) observe execution feedback, forming an interaction trajectory until the task is solved. Unlike retrieval-pipeline methods, ToolWeaver unifies selection and execution inside one fine-tuned LLM (Llama-3-8B primary; Qwen series in appendix) that natively generates hierarchical code-token sequences for tools, removing the external retriever. Supervision is available: query-tool pairs for retrieval alignment and full ToolBench trajectories for trajectory alignment.
what_is_retrieved: Tools / APIs. Each tool is represented and 'retrieved' as a generated hierarchical sequence of discrete code-tokens (e.g., <T1_1><T2_2>) rather than a flat tool ID; the LLM generates the code sequence identifying the tool to invoke.
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus: the frozen ToolBench/RapidAPI pool of 46,985 APIs encoded once (offline) into a fixed compositional code space (L=2 codebooks x K=1024 codes). No growing/episodic memory is written at test time; the codebook and trie of valid tool codes are fixed after offline tokenization and fine-tuning.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Hybrid. For tool retrieval evaluation the objective is a top-k generative ranking (reported via NDCG@{1,3,5}). For end-to-end multi-tool tasks (I2/I3) the agent must recover and orchestrate the complete set of tools needed across a trajectory, so completeness of the multi-tool selection matters; selection per step is generative (one tool code sequence at a time via constrained beam search).
cbr_cycle_coverage: Not a CBR work. If forced to map: [Retrieve: partial - generates tool identities, not prior cases; Reuse: no; Revise: no; Retain: no]. N/A.
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The paper does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner; it is framed as generative tool learning with collaborative-aware structured tokenization (RQ-VAE) inspired by generative recommendation (LC-Rec) and residual quantization.
retrieval_unit: tool-API, but represented as a compositional sequence of L discrete codes (a hierarchical code path through L=2 codebooks, e.g., <T1_*><T2_*>). The retrievable unit is the structured code sequence uniquely identifying one ToolBench API; shared parent codes group functionally/collaboratively related tools.
index_source: Static corpus, offline-induced: the 46,985-API ToolBench corpus is encoded offline by collaborative-aware residual quantization (RQ-VAE) into a fixed set of L*K=2048 code-tokens. The co-occurrence/similarity matrix used during codebook learning is mined offline from ToolBench usage trajectories. Not online/test-time-induced; the store is frozen after offline training.
index_structure_topology: Hierarchical / compositional code tree: each tool maps to a length-L code path over L=2 codebooks (each K=1024), forming a prefix-tree (trie) of valid code sequences. Functionally/collaboratively related tools share higher-level (parent) codes (e.g., Realtime Weather=<T1_1><T2_1> and Air Quality=<T1_1><T2_2> share <T1_1>), giving a category->finer-distinction hierarchy emerging from residual quantization rather than a flat vector index.
retriever_type: Generative (tool-as-token / tool-as-code-sequence): the LLM itself generates the hierarchical code sequence for the target tool (no separate dense/sparse retriever). Baselines span BM25, dense embedding similarity (EmbSim), supervised dense retriever (ToolRetriever), and atomic-token generative (ToolGen).
retriever_learning_signal: Two-part learned signal. (1) Codebook/tokenizer learning: unsupervised RQ-VAE objective combining reconstruction + quantization (commitment) loss with an additional graph-Laplacian collaborative regularization L_collab driven by a tool-tool co-occurrence similarity matrix A (lambda=1.0 optimal), plus Sinkhorn-Knopp optimal-transport uniform-mapping constraint on the final codebook for conflict mitigation. (2) Generative alignment: supervised next-token cross-entropy fine-tuning of the LLM to produce tool code sequences (Stage 1 retrieval alignment) and full trajectories (Stage 2). No RL (RL is named only as future work).
query_construction: Raw user query q is used directly as the conditioning input; the fine-tuned LLM generates the tool's code sequence P(iota_d | q) (Stage 1) or interleaves reasoning, tool code-tokens, and parameters within a trajectory (Stage 2). No explicit query decomposition or synthetic-query expansion of the query at inference.
query_granularity: Both task-level and step-level. Stage-1 retrieval alignment is query-level (q -> tool code sequence). Stage-2 trajectory alignment is step/state-level: at each agent step the model conditions on the running context to generate the next tool's code sequence and parameters.
when_to_retrieve: Iterative within a trajectory: tool selection (code-sequence generation) occurs at each action step of the agent's reasoning-acting loop. There is no separate uncertainty-triggered or learned router; tool generation is woven into autoregressive decoding whenever an action/tool call is produced.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed/structural: tool selection is triggered by the autoregressive generation reaching an action/tool-call position in the trajectory; at that point constrained (trie-guided) beam search forces a valid tool code sequence. No token-confidence, attention-uncertainty, learned complexity classifier, or reflection-token trigger.
reranking: No explicit reranking stage. Selection is done by constrained beam search over the hierarchical code trie (masking logits of invalid next code-tokens) rather than scoring and reranking a candidate list.
retrieved_context_refinement: None in the classic sense (no rerank/distill/compress of retrieved documents). The relevant processing is on the index side: collaborative-aware residual quantization plus Sinkhorn-Knopp uniform-mapping to mitigate code collisions; at inference, trie-constrained decoding ensures only valid tool codes are produced.
tool_document_engineering: Tool name + description documentation is encoded by a pretrained text encoder (all-mpnet-base-v2, 768-d) into an initial semantic embedding, then projected (MLP to 64-d) and quantized via collaborative-aware RQ-VAE. The codes thus 'weave' intrinsic semantics (text embedding) with extrinsic co-usage (co-occurrence similarity matrix A). No synthetic-query augmentation; instead structured-tokenization with collaborative regularization.
index_content_separation: Partial: a lightweight compositional code identifier (L*K=2048 added tokens; logarithmic vs linear vocab growth) stands in for the heavy per-tool documentation. The trie of valid code sequences is the retrievable index; full tool docs are not loaded into the LLM context at selection time (the tool is generated as codes). Not a progressive SOP-index-then-content scheme.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: Static tool index (frozen ToolBench/RapidAPI pool of 46,985 APIs encoded once into codebooks). Integration/execution protocol is RapidAPI via the StableToolBench framework; no live CRUD auto-sync and no MCP. Adding new tools would require re-running/extending tokenization (logarithmic vocab growth makes this cheaper than atomic methods, but it is not live-synchronized).
tool_dependency_awareness: Yes, implicitly via collaborative co-usage. A tool-tool co-occurrence matrix C (counts of tools appearing together in usage trajectories) yields a cosine similarity matrix A used in a graph-Laplacian collaborative regularization L_collab, so frequently co-used tools share parent codes and the model learns collaborative patterns from dense shared-code co-occurrence. This models co-usage / collaborative relationships rather than an explicit output-of-A-feeds-B dependency graph or shared-auth prerequisites.
how_retrieved_used: Generative selection + execution: the LLM natively generates the tool's hierarchical code-token sequence (decoded back to the tool/API) plus its parameters within reasoning trajectories, then the tool is invoked (RapidAPI via StableToolBench). Tool knowledge is injected as new vocabulary code-tokens learned during generative alignment, not as prompt-context tool documents.
planning_integration: Per-step interleaved generative tool calling within the agent's reasoning-acting trajectory: the model produces reasoning, then a tool call (code-tokens + parameters), observes feedback, and repeats. Trained via Stage-2 trajectory alignment on full ToolBench trajectories; tool selection is fused into autoregressive planning rather than a separate retrieve-then-plan pipeline. No explicit MCTS/tree search over plans (constrained beam search is only over the tool-code trie at selection).
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-tool-call within a rollout: each action step in the trajectory emits a tool code sequence interleaved with reasoning and parameters; not per-CoT-token retrieval.
retrieved_item_representation: Latent-soft / structured code-tokens: tools are injected as hierarchical sequences of newly added vocabulary tokens (L*K=2048 codes) with randomly initialized, then fine-tuned embeddings. The surface form generated is the code sequence (e.g., <T1_1><T2_2>) standing for an executable API, not raw trajectories or free-text workflows.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Procedural tool / executable API, but represented at a structured compositional abstraction: a hierarchical code path where higher-level codes denote coarse functional/collaborative groupings and lower-level codes denote finer distinctions on the residual.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Index-side structural robustness rather than retrieved-context filtering: (1) collaborative-aware regularization balances intrinsic semantics vs co-usage (lambda=1.0 optimal; too large distorts representations); (2) Sinkhorn-Knopp uniform-mapping mitigates index collisions; (3) trie-constrained beam search guarantees only valid tool codes are generated, preventing hallucinated/invalid tool identifiers. No retriever-aware distractor SFT or self-reflection relevance evaluator.
memory_type: None (no persistent/episodic memory). Tool knowledge is amortized into fixed codebook embeddings and LLM weights; there is no test-time-growing experience store.
write_back: False: the system does not write new experiences/cases/skills into a growing memory during deployment. The codebooks and tool-code vocabulary are fixed after offline tokenization and fine-tuning.
online_growth: No: the retrievable store (tool-code space / trie) is frozen after offline induction; it does not grow at test time. (The compositional design makes future offline expansion logarithmic, but this is not online growth.)
write_back_trigger: Never (no write-back). Learning is entirely offline: codebook training plus two-stage supervised fine-tuning; nothing is written to a durable store at inference.
failure_experience_usage: Not used at inference for memory. Failures are only analyzed post-hoc (Appendix B.8 failure taxonomy: Wrong Tool dominant, rising 71%->95% from I1->I3; Wrong Parameters, Incomplete/Redundant Process). No success/failure experiences are stored or retrieved; co-usage signal is mined from (presumably successful) usage trajectories offline.
memory_evolution_update: N/A / append-only-offline: codebook entries are learned once offline and not mutated during deployment; no delta-update, forgetting, or link-and-evolve at test time.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: Partially: tool selection is a learned generative model (LLM fine-tuned to generate tool code sequences) plus a learned tokenizer (RQ-VAE with collaborative regularization), so it is not a fixed similarity top-k. However it is NOT an RL/value-based policy (no M-MDP/soft-Q/RL); selection is supervised next-token generation with trie-constrained decoding. RL is named only as future work.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No: single-model, single-agent. Tool knowledge is private to the fine-tuned LLM's weights/codebook; no cross-agent or cross-framework memory sharing.
benchmarks: ToolBench (Qin et al., 2023; 46,985 APIs, 129 tool collections, 49 functional categories; standardized 641-query test set; scenarios I1 single-tool, I2 intra-category multi-tool, I3 intra-collection multi-tool; generalization splits I1-Tool, I1-Cat, I2-Cat). End-to-end via StableToolBench framework. General-capability evaluation: WikiText-2 (perplexity), CNN/DailyMail and XSum (summarization BERTScore), plus MMLU and additional benchmarks in Appendix B.4. Qwen2.5 results in Appendix B.3.
benchmark_family: tool (ToolBench / RapidAPI tool-use; StableToolBench evaluation). Auxiliary: general-LM benchmarks (WikiText-2 LM perplexity; CNN/DM, XSum summarization; MMLU understanding).
baselines: Retrieval: BM25, Embedding Similarity (EmbSim, OpenAI text-embedding-3-large), ToolRetriever (supervised BERT dense retriever), ToolGen (atomic-token generative). End-to-end: GPT-4o-mini (retrieval setting; also SoWR reference model), ToolLlama-2 (retrieval setting), ToolGen, ToolWeaver. Additional retrieval baselines in appendix: Re-Invoke, IterFeedback. Tokenization-strategy ablation baselines: Atomic (as ToolGen), Numerical, Hierarchical (clustering-based), Semantic (lexicon-based).
key_metrics: Tool retrieval: NDCG@{1,3,5}. End-to-end agent: Solvable Pass Rate (SoPR) and Solvable Win Rate (SoWR, computed against GPT-4o-mini reference) under StableToolBench. General capability: Perplexity (WikiText-2), Summarization BERTScore F1 (CNN/DM, XSum), and average drop. Efficiency: avg/P95 latency (ms), throughput (Tok/s), peak GPU memory (GB).
headline_result: On ToolBench, ToolWeaver outperforms SOTA across tool retrieval and end-to-end tasks with ~46,985 tools. Retrieval: I3 NDCG@1 = 88.00 vs ToolGen 81.00 (and I1 NDCG@1 91.16, I2 89.76). End-to-end I3 SoPR = 52.19 vs ToolGen 36.34, and I3 SoWR = 59.02 vs ToolGen 49.18. It also preserves general language ability far better: WikiText-2 PPL 25.36 vs ToolGen 104.54 (base 6.34), summarization avg drop 0.57 vs ToolGen 2.47.
ablations: (1) Collaborative regularization weight lambda: avg NDCG@k across I1-I3 peaks at lambda=1 (improves from 0.01->1, declines at 10), validating intrinsic-vs-collaborative balance. (2) Component ablation (cumulative): w/o semantic initialization (baseline) -> adding semantic initialization gives >20 NDCG-point jump -> adding collaborative guidance gives a further gain that scales with task complexity (largest for I3). (3) Tokenization strategy comparison: ToolWeaver > Atomic (ToolGen), Numerical, Hierarchical (clustering), Semantic (lexicon) on both retrieval and SoPR/SoWR; naive structured methods (Hierarchical/Semantic) fail to beat the Atomic baseline end-to-end. (4) General-capability impact: ToolWeaver vastly less degradation than ToolGen (PPL 25.36 vs 104.54). (5) Appendix: codebook vocab/code-length sensitivity (B.5), Sinkhorn-Knopp efficiency/entropy-eps ablation (B.6), inference latency/memory by depth L (B.7), failure analysis (B.8).
evaluation_decoupling: Yes: intrinsic retrieval ranking metrics (NDCG@{1,3,5}, Tables 1) are reported separately from end-to-end agent task metrics (SoPR/SoWR, Table 2), and general-LM metrics are reported separately (Table 3).
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Both. Outcome: SoPR (task completion) and SoWR (answer quality). Process: intrinsic retrieval NDCG@k (selection quality), plus a failure-mode taxonomy over trajectories (Process Consistency: Redundant/Incomplete Process; Wrong Tool; Wrong Parameters) in Appendix B.8.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Inference efficiency analyzed (Appendix B.7, A100-80GB, K=1024): vs ToolGen atomic (avg latency 108.16 ms, throughput 19.54 Tok/s, peak mem 15.77 GB), ToolWeaver L=2 = 128.21 ms (~20 ms overhead), 24.53 Tok/s, 15.08 GB; L=3 = 157.65 ms, 26.34 Tok/s, 15.10 GB; L=4 = 183.14 ms (<200 ms), 28.26 Tok/s, 15.11 GB. Latency grows linearly with depth L but absolute overhead (~20-75 ms) is negligible vs external API call times; higher token throughput at larger L; memory ~constant and ~0.67 GB lower than ToolGen (logarithmic L*K=2048 vs ~47k atomic tokens). Sinkhorn-Knopp cost analyzed in B.6.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Tool selection uses constrained beam search over the code trie; each tool decoded as an L-length code sequence (L=2 main, L*K=2048 added tokens). Training input context truncated to 6,144 tokens. Retrieval reported at fixed k for NDCG@{1,3,5}; per-step a single tool code sequence is generated (not a large candidate list injected into context), avoiding the input-length pressure of retrieval-pipeline baselines.
benchmark_construction_and_size: Uses existing ToolBench (Qin et al., 2023), not a new benchmark: 46,985 real-world RapidAPI APIs, 129 tool collections, 49 functional categories; standardized 641-query test set across I1/I2/I3 with generalization splits (I1-Tool, I1-Cat, I2-Cat). Training data adapted to generative codes: 489,702 query-tool pairs (Stage 1) and 183,336 full trajectories (Stage 2). Answer verifiability via StableToolBench (SoPR/SoWR vs GPT-4o-mini reference). Difficulty signal: best system (ToolWeaver) I3 SoPR 52.19, I3 SoWR 59.02.
builds_on: ToolGen (Wang et al., 2024b; atomic-token generative tool calling, which ToolWeaver directly extends/replaces with compositional codes); ToolLLM/ToolBench and ToolRetriever (Qin et al., 2023; corpus, retriever, ToolLlama, evaluation); StableToolBench (Guo et al., 2024; SoPR/SoWR evaluation). Tokenization machinery: RQ-VAE residual quantization (Lee et al., 2022), LC-Rec collaborative-semantic generative IDs and uniform mapping (Zheng et al., 2024), Sinkhorn-Knopp optimal transport (Cuturi, 2013); ToolkenGPT (Hao et al., 2023) tool-as-token precursor; Llama-3-8B (Dubey et al., 2024) and Qwen2.5 (Yang et al., 2025) backbones; all-mpnet-base-v2 / Sentence-Transformers encoder.
contrasts_with: Retrieval-pipeline tool selection (BM25, EmbSim, ToolRetriever, Re-Invoke, IterFeedback, Gorilla, ToolLLM) which suffer latency/complexity and context-length limits; atomic one-token-per-tool generative methods (ToolGen, ToolkenGPT) which cause linear vocab explosion (~47k OOV tokens), catastrophic general-LM degradation, and a semantic bottleneck from sparse monolithic-ID co-occurrence; and naive structured tokenizations (Numerical, clustering-based Hierarchical, lexicon-based Semantic) that fail to beat the Atomic baseline. Also contrasts with post-hoc collaborative-alignment methods (SeLLa-Rec, LC-Rec, GAL-Rec, CFRAG) by weaving collaborative semantics into the tokenization itself rather than aligning isolated IDs afterward.
lineage: Group E (tool-use). Lineage: generative tool calling (ToolkenGPT -> ToolGen tool-as-token) evolved to compositional/hierarchical tool-as-code-sequence; ToolWeaver fuses generative-recommendation-style collaborative-aware RQ-VAE tokenization (LC-Rec, RQ-VAE, Sinkhorn-Knopp) with LLM tool learning, targeting extreme-scale (~47k tools) logarithmic vocab growth and collaborative multi-tool orchestration. Concurrent/related: ToolScaler (Su et al., 2025; structure-aware semantic tokenization for scalable generative tool calling).
